summary: Connection leak keeping GPU slots reserved and triggering autoscale shortfall in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaHealth reports persistent elevated p50/p99 latency and a degradation in throughput on their dedicated GPU pool during weekday business hours. Symptoms correspond to GPUs remaining attached/occupied for long periods even after clients close streams.

Impact:
- LexaHealth production traffic experiences 30-60% throughput degradation for batched routes and repeated autoscale down-failures.
- Automated fallback to lower-tier model variants has been observed but does not restore throughput due to slot reservation.
- Customer SLAs degraded; they are an important health-care partner (sensitive workloads).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: lexah-health-dedicated-prod (us-west-2)
- Runtime version: 2026.02.11-rc3
- Autoscaler: predictive-v2 (configured min: 2, max: 24)
- Scheduler/allocator: allocator-1.9.4

Steps to reproduce (replicated internally):
1) Send a sequence of long-lived streaming calls (keep-alive with no data for 45s) from a synthetic client matching LexaHealth traffic patterns (n=150 streams over 10m).
2) Close TCP connection abruptly on client side for ~30% of connections.
3) Observe connection/slot state in allocator and GPU attachment list.

Observed behavior:
- Several GPU slots show "attached" but have no active inference threads and show stale KV cache leases.
- Autoscaler fails to shrink because allocator reports slots in-use; new allocations are delayed and queue grows.
- p50 increases by ~120ms, p99 by ~800ms; throughput (requests/minute) drops ~40% relative to baseline.
- Monitoring shows high ephemeral socket counts on serving runtime sidecar and open file descriptors not reclaimed.

Expected behavior:
- Closed/aborted client connections should free associated slot leases quickly (within 3s). Autoscaler should be able to scale down when unused capacity is available and not blocked by leaked reservations.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Sample serving sidecar stacktrace: "runtime/connection: reclaim loop stuck waiting on lease-release for 00:12:34" (attached in support artifact).
- Allocator metric: slot_reserved_count spikes and does not fall for 10+ minutes after clients close.
- Kernel-level socket states show many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on sidecar.

Initial customer report (excerpt):
"We see our RL training jobs starve the dedicated pool in the morning window. It looks like slots are being held even though inference calls finished — this started last Wed after a deploy. Can you help?" — LexaHealth SRE
comments: 2026-03-10 08:45 — Aisha Kumar (Support): Ticket created after initial customer report. Notified SRE and Engineering on #support and #dedicated-pools.
2026-03-10 09:10 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Began triage. Reproduced slot reservation pattern in a sandbox. Collected allocator and sidecar heap profiles.

2026-03-10 11:02 — Priya Nair (Eng, serving-runtime): Observed socket CLOSE_WAIT buildup in sidecar logs. Hypothesis: a race during abrupt client disconnect leaves lease token unreturned to allocator.

2026-03-10 13:30 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Deployed temporary aggressive TTL reclamation to one reserve pool (lexah-health-dedicated-prod-agg1) as a mitigation. Observed partial recovery of throughput (~20% improvement) but some slots remained reserved.

2026-03-11 09:50 — LexaHealth SRE: Confirmed reduced impact with mitigation but requested permanent fix. Provided additional connection traces and a sample of client SDK behavior (abrupt closes after heartbeat failure).

2026-03-11 14:20 — Priya Nair (Eng): Created PR to add explicit lease cleanup on connection finalizers and added metrics around lease handoff. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/8921

2026-03-12 07:40 — Diego Martinez (SRE): Running load test with PR branch; observed near-complete slot reclamation within 5s on abrupt disconnects. Preparing rollout plan for canary on lexah-health pool.
2026-03-12 13:05 — Aisha Kumar (Support): Informed customer of progress and planned canary rollout this evening. SLA remediation discussion scheduled if regression persists.
investigation_notes: Heap/profile analysis shows sidecar not entering connection finalizer when client TCP FIN is missing; sockets linger in CLOSE_WAIT.
Allocator only accepts lease release events from sidecar — if sidecar finalizer does not run, allocator considers slot in-use.
Repeatable with synthetic client that mirrors LexaHealth SDK abrupt-close behavior; not limited to a specific model but amplified for large KV caches (long context models).
Temporary TTL reclamation improved availability but is a blunt instrument and risks premature eviction of genuinely warm slots.
resolution_notes: Mitigation: Enabled aggressive lease TTL reclamation for affected pool (lexah-health-dedicated-prod-agg1) at 2026-03-10 13:30 — partial throughput recovery.
Fix in progress: PR to add explicit lease cleanup on sidecar connection finalizers and defensive GC for orphaned leases (allocator PR #8921).

Rollout plan: Canary deploy fix to 5% of lexah pool traffic on 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC; monitor slot_reserved_count, p99 latency, and socket CLOSE_WAIT metrics for 2 hours. If stable, ramp to 100% over 4 hours.
Follow-ups: Add automated test for abrupt-close scenarios in our integration harness; add monitor alert for slot_reserved_count > threshold to trigger auto-ttl escalation with a safe floor.
